data.name: Hukum
data.gender_notes: Hukum is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit root ‘huk’ meaning ‘to order’ or ‘command’. The name Hukum signifies a powerful authority or ruler. In Hindu mythology, the term Hukum is used to refer to the divine will, the ultimate authority and the supreme ruler of the universe. The name Hukum carries the meaning “Lord, Master” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Hukum usually hope their child will grow to embody lord, master and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes submission to the divine will.
data.etymology: Hukum belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord, Master.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hukum total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Hukum carries a significant cultural impact, evoking a sense of power, strength, and authority in traditional Hindu society. It is a name that is often held in high regard, symbolizing leadership and influence. Historically, this name was given to rulers and other influential figures in Hindu communities.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Hukum reflects the belief in the ultimate authority and divine will of the universe. It serves as a reminder of the interconnectedness of all things and the presence of a higher power guiding our lives. In Hindu philosophy, surrendering to the Hukum (divine will) is considered a noble pursuit, as it leads to inner peace and harmony.
